transcript:
[00:00] Jordan Lee: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. uh this is Jordan from Redwood, I'm the AE on the account. We also have Priya, our solutions engineer.
[00:06] Priya Patel: Hi all, Priya here. We'll try to keep this focused on scope and timeline for the POC.
[00:11] Samir Patel: Thanks, Jordan. Quick intros: Marta runs ML, Elliot platform infra. We're evaluating inference options, want to scope a POC to validate latencies and cost at our scale.
[00:20] Jordan Lee: Great, can you share the primary success criteria? like what would make this a yes for you?
[00:26] Marta Ruiz: Sure, three things: one, p95 latency under 300ms for our 256 token median prompt, two, throughput to support ~50 concurrent sessions with spikes to 200 qps, and three, cost that aligns to under $0.50 per 1k generated tokens - roughly, ballpark. Also minimal regression on accuracy, we have some internal eval tests.
[00:45] Priya Patel: Ok that's helpful. Couple clarifying q's: when you say 50 concurrent sessions, is that steady or expected peak?
[00:50] Marta Ruiz: 50 steady, peaks to 200 qps during campaign windows, so we need to test both steady-state and burst behavior.
[00:57] Priya Patel: Got it. And token lengths? you mentioned 256 median - what's the 95th?
[01:02] Marta Ruiz: 95th is about 1024, so we should test on 256/1024 distributions.
[01:08] Jordan Lee: Great. On the Redwood side we'll recommend a few model configs - a quantized 4-bit for cost tests and a float16 variant for latency/quality trade-offs. We'll also look at batching and KV cache settings.
[01:18] Samir Patel: Can you remind me about Redwood Dedicated vs hosted? we care about isolation but also cost.
[01:23] Priya Patel: Yeah, so hosted API is simplest and quick, Dedicated gives you reserved GPU pools and better isolation. For POC we usually start on our hosted but with dedicated-like configs; if you need full VPC/private networking we can spin up a private eval cluster, but that takes a few extra days for network setup.
[01:39] Elliot Chen: We will likely need VPC peering and SSO; our security team requires audit logs and KMS integration.
[01:45] Jordan Lee: That's fine. We'll include our security pack: SOC2 docs, KMS HSM options, and audit logging. Priya, can you capture the access/setup steps?
[01:54] Priya Patel: Sure. Typical flow: 1) exchange network requirements and open peering, 2) share service account with least-priv permissions, 3) Redwood provisions eval endpoints, 4) we run an initial smoke test and baseline benchmarks. If VPC is needed add 1-2 business days for peering and firewall exceptions.
[02:11] Marta Ruiz: Ok timeline wise what are we looking at? we want an exec readout in ~6 weeks.
[02:17] Jordan Lee: We usually do a 6-week POC: Week 0 kickoff and access, Week 1 baseline + initial benchmarks, Week 2-3 tuning and workload runs, Week 3 midpoint review, Week 4-5 extended stress tests and regression evals, Week 6 exec readout.
[02:33] Samir Patel: That aligns. Can you define the midpoint deliverables?
[02:37] Priya Patel: Mid-point review will include: measured p95 latency and p50, throughput/saturation curves, cost estimates per 1M tokens under the tested config, and a quality regression report against your eval set. We'll also surface tuning levers: batching, KV cache hit rates, quantization impacts.
[02:55] Marta Ruiz: For benchmarks we want: cold start latency, warm p95, steady-state throughput, and token-level cost. Also characterize tail latency under burst.
[03:04] Priya Patel: We'll script a suite: load generator with your token distribution, warm and cold runs, and an end-to-end app flow test to capture real API behavior including streaming if you use it.
[03:13] Elliot Chen: How do you handle cost calculations across variants? we need a clear apples-to-apples.
[03:17] Jordan Lee: We'll produce a normalized cost model: tokens, model size, and GPU-hour effective rates. For the POC we show per-1M token cost for each variant and include estimated infra overhead.
[03:26] Marta Ruiz: Good. Security checklist? we need SAML SSO, enterprise audit logs, and contractual data retention terms.
[03:33] Jordan Lee: We'll send SSO instructions, and include SOC2, ISO docs. If you need private deployment we'll cover KMS/HSM integrations and on-prem options but that adds time.
[03:43] Samir Patel: Ok noted. Any dependencies from our side?
[03:46] Priya Patel: The key items: sample traffic logs, a representative prompt set for quality evals, and network contact for peering. Also a list of stakeholder attendees for the mid-point and exec readouts.
[03:58] Marta Ruiz: We can provide logs and eval prompts by Friday.
[04:01] Jordan Lee: Excellent. On timing we'll plan kickoff next Tuesday, May 27th. Access setup within 3 business days of kickoff, then baseline benchmarks within the first week, midpoint review on week 3, and exec readout in week 6.
[04:14] Elliot Chen: That schedule looks doable. Can you also include a checklist for the engineers to follow?
[04:18] Priya Patel: Yes, I'll include a runbook: how to hit the endpoints, env vars, expected flags, and the benchmark script with parameters.
[04:25] Marta Ruiz: For success criteria, reiterating: p95 < 300ms for 256 median, throughput to handle 50 concurrency and spikes to 200 qps, cost target under $0.50/1k tokens, and no more than 2% regression on key accuracy metrics.
[04:40] Jordan Lee: Perfect. We'll include those as pass/fail gates in the POC doc. Anything else?
[04:44] Samir Patel: Please include how caching affects stateful sessions and KV cache sizing — we use a lot of context caching.
[04:52] Priya Patel: We'll capture KV cache sizing recommendations and note impact on warm p95 vs cold. Also will include quantization tradeoffs and observed quality deltas.
[05:01] Marta Ruiz: Ok. Let's recap next steps.
[05:04] Jordan Lee: Recap: Jordan to send POC doc + timeline and security pack; Priya to provision eval infra and benchmark scripts; Orchard to send sample logs and prompts; schedule mid-point and exec readout.
[05:17] Elliot Chen: I'll route the peering request to our networking team today.
[05:20] Jordan Lee: Thanks everyone. We'll follow up with the email and the doc.
[05:23] Samir Patel: Thanks, talk soon.
[05:25] [call ends]
notes: Represents a typical Redwood-led POC scoping call. References to product names may be transcribed imperfectly (e.g., KV cache as 'K V cache'). Links mentioned: POC plan (link to deck), security pack (link to docs), benchmark spreadsheet (link).
